tasks.short: Hand out and score the questionnaire on feelings and behaviours, ask questions in session, and decide what to explore next.

steps.what: Client fills the questionnaire on feelings and behaviours in the client portal before the session
Family therapist hands out and scores a paper questionnaire today; after the change, reads the portal scores and the change since last time, and hands out paper to clients without the portal
Family therapist asks questions that help clients identify their feelings and behaviours
Family therapist decides which feelings and behaviours to explore next

tasks.design: Clients fill the questionnaire on feelings and behaviours in the client portal before the session ({OTHER}), which scores it and shows the change since last time, so the therapist does not hand it out and score it by hand. Asking questions and choosing what to explore stay with the therapist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Questionnaires were on paper and scored by hand in the session.
tasks.enabler_now: Client portals send and score questionnaires.
tasks.still_hard: Some clients will not fill anything in before a session.
tasks.human_edge: Asking the question a family has been avoiding.

reach.learn: Whether the questionnaire helps them reflect.

evidence.claim: Client portals can send questionnaires and score them.
Health data are special category data under the GDPR.

assumptions: Boundary: from the session due to the focus decided; treatment planning is outside.
Input contract: clients have portal access; fallback is the paper questionnaire.
Questioning in the session does not change.

Clients fill the questionnaire at home (s0); their time is outside the therapist's savings and is not counted again as new work. The portal scores the questionnaire by its fixed key; no AI scores the client.
research_questions: Do clients who fill it in beforehand get further in sessions?

incremental.description: Family therapist reminds clients to fill the questionnaire.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: about half of clients do not use the portal, so s1 keeps 60 (5.1); high: most clients fill it in before the session (9.3).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Coach clients in skills and strategies in session, prepare exercise sheets, and answer clients' questions about exercises between sessions.

steps.what: Family therapist encourages individuals and family members to develop and use skills for confronting their problems
Family therapist prepares exercise sheets and handouts for practice at home
Client opens the exercise sheets and videos in the client portal at home
Family therapist answers clients' e-mails about exercises between sessions

tasks.design: A library of exercise sheets and short videos per skill sits in the client portal ({OTHER}); the therapist picks and adjusts one for the family instead of making a handout each time. The instructions and videos answer common questions, so fewer e-mails come between sessions. Coaching in session stays with the therapist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Handouts were made per family and questions came by e-mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Client portals hold exercise libraries with videos.
tasks.still_hard: Families in crisis do not do exercises at home.
tasks.human_edge: Getting a couple to try a new way of arguing.

evidence.claim: Client portals can hold exercise libraries with sheets and videos that therapists assign.

assumptions: Boundary: from the session due to questions answered; treatment planning is outside.
Input contract: exercise library kept by the practice; fallback is handouts.
Coaching in session does not change.

Clients use the portal at home (s2a); their time is outside the therapist's savings and is not counted again as new work. s2 keeps 60 because the therapist still picks and adjusts each exercise for the family.
research_questions: Do families practise more between sessions?

incremental.description: Family therapist adds and updates exercises in the library.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many families prefer paper and keep mailing questions, so s2 keeps 80 and s3 keeps 90 (4.3); high: library and videos as designed (10.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review intake information, develop the treatment plan with the client, write it, evaluate progress against its goals, and update the plan.

steps.what: Family therapist reviews intake information, referral letter and assessments
Family therapist develops the individualised treatment plan with the client
Family therapist writes the treatment plan document
Family therapist implements the plan by evaluating progress against its goals with the client
Family therapist updates the treatment plan

tasks.design: The client file ({OTHER}) shows the referral letter, intake answers and questionnaire scores on one screen, so the therapist does not gather them from letters and forms. The treatment plan is a form in the file with fields for problems, goals, interventions and review dates, filled from the intake where possible; updates change only the fields that changed. Developing the plan with the client and evaluating progress stay with the therapist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Intake information was spread over letters and forms and plans were written as free text.
tasks.enabler_now: Client files hold structured treatment plans and intake data.
tasks.still_hard: Families with many problems do not fit a standard form.
tasks.human_edge: Agreeing goals that every family member can accept.

evidence.claim: Client files can hold structured treatment plans with goals and review dates.
The treatment file is kept twenty years after the last change.

assumptions: Boundary: from the intake done to the plan updated; sessions are outside.
Input contract: intake forms and letters stored in the file; fallback is paper.

Planning decisions stay with the therapist and client. s3 keeps 75 because the therapist writes the problems, goals and interventions; the form fills details from the intake and gives the layout. s5 keeps 75 because unchanged parts are no longer retyped; the changes are still written.
research_questions: Are plans reviewed on time more often?

incremental.description: Family therapist adds free text where the form does not fit.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: families with many problems, where much intake information sits outside the file and the plan is mostly free text, so s1 keeps 80 and s3 keeps 90 (8.0); high: file and form as designed (15.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Write progress notes after sessions, write evaluations and recommendations, register sessions, file letters, and check the file before closing.

steps.what: Family therapist asks the client's consent to record the session and starts the recording
Family therapist writes progress notes after each session

loop.input: The session recording transcript, made with the clients' consent.
loop.output: A draft progress note in the file's note fields.
loop.check: A validator flags any risk statement about self-harm, violence or child safety and any statement not found in the transcript. The therapist reads every note against the transcript and what happened in the session, checks that it says what was said and nothing more, and edits it before it is saved; unclear passages are written by hand.
loop.stop: One draft per session; if rejected, the therapist writes the note.
loop.why_not_simpler: Dictation still leaves the therapist to compose the whole note.

steps.what: Family therapist evaluates the client's progress and decides the recommendations
Family therapist writes evaluations and recommendations in the template that fills goals and scores
Family therapist marks the appointment held and confirms the actual session time and activities; the registration is filled from it
Family therapist files letters and documents in the case file
Family therapist checks the case file for completeness before closing

tasks.design: For clients who consent to recording, a scribe in the client file ({OTHER}) drafts the progress note from the session transcript; risk statements and anything not in the transcript are flagged, and the therapist edits and validates every note. Evaluations use a template that fills goals and questionnaire scores from the file, and the therapist writes the assessment and recommendations. Sessions are registered from the agenda when the therapist marks the appointment held and confirms the actual time and activities, and incoming letters from the secure mail system are linked to the file. Checking the file before closing stays with the therapist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Notes were typed after sessions and registration done by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Care scribes draft notes from recordings for the clinician to validate.
tasks.still_hard: Scribe drafts of emotional family sessions can miss who said what.
tasks.human_edge: Writing a note that is honest and that the family could read.
tasks.altitude: The therapist validates notes instead of typing them.

evidence.claim: Attendi turns spoken notes into a SOEP report or letter in the care record for over 300 care organisations.
Somerset Council's children's social care pilot of Magic Notes reported about 11 hours a week saved per practitioner, self-reported.
Health data are special category data under the GDPR.
The treatment file is kept twenty years after the last change.

assumptions: Boundary: from the session held to the file complete; billing is outside.
Input contract: scribe set up in the client file; fallback is typing notes.
Scenario: about 70% of clients consent to recording; for the rest the therapist writes notes as today.

The therapist validates every note. s3 keeps 75 because the therapist writes the assessment and recommendations; the template fills goals and scores. s4 keeps 30 for confirming the actual time and activities of each session.
research_questions: How long does validating a drafted family session note take?

already_counted.description: Family therapist edits and validates drafted notes.

incremental.description: No new work: asking consent is shown as step s0.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: only half of clients consent to recording, so s1 keeps 68 (32.5); high: about 70% consent as assumed (38.3).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The family therapist keeps asking, coaching, planning with clients and validating notes; scoring questionnaires, making handouts, gathering intake papers and typing notes shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A therapist with more time for families.
